raw_comment:
The first thing I noticed was the large exceptional drought in the Southwest part of Texas under New Mexico. I noticed how it stands out compared to the rest of the droughts in the U.S. because most of the exceptional droughts are more in the landlocked areas of the U.S. like Wyoming or Montana.
I wonder how people in areas with exceptional or severe droughts conserve their water or water usage. I also wonder what protection those areas have for their water reservoirs, so they don't completely evaporate due to the intense heat.
This relates to me and my community because I haven't seen much rain or form of precipitation in my area. A severe drought here could damage my area a ton considering the fact that we don't usually get droughts in Long Island, and because we usually don't get droughts, we wouldn't have proper protection and safety measured put in place in the case of a severe or exceptional drought occurring.
A catchy headline for this graph could be, "America is drying up like a sponge!"
